title: A Ember for the Thorn Again
premise: Theo Thornbury has spent their whole life in Hollowmere, a valley where magic cannot follow, hiding the fact that they are the last swordspeaker—an oath-bound mage whose words can wake steel. When the crown's witch-hunters breach the valley hunting the gift, Theo learns their late mentor hid an ember of the old war-magic inside them, and that the hunters' captain is hunting it to finish what the ancient war started. Fleeing with two unlikely companions—a disgraced royal cartographer and a mute child who remembers too much—Theo must decide whether to destroy the ember or speak it awake. In the end, Theo speaks a new oath that unbinds the ember and scatters its power into every blade in the realm, ending both the hunt and the war's long shadow, though they lose their own magic—and gain, at last, a family that chose them.
about_author: Rafael Marchetti is a former archivist of oral histories who writes fantasy about the stories people refuse to let die. They live in a coastal town where they collect broken clocks and insist each one still tells the truth twice a day.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Establishes Hollowmere's quiet rhythms and Theo's careful invisibility: no oaths spoken aloud, blades left unwoken. A traveling peddler recognizes a swordspeaker's sigil on Theo's knife hilt and leaves in a hurry. Emotional beat: the loneliness of being unseen even by those you love.

chapters.title: Riders at the Ford
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Crown hunters arrive at the valley's edge, led by Captain Vess Arden, whose cold courtesy terrifies more than threats would. The village elders lie for Theo—badly. Theo realizes the peddler sold them out. Emotional beat: fear curdling into guilt as neighbors risk themselves for a secret Theo never chose to share.

chapters.title: What My Mentor Buried
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, flashback-woven. Searching their dead mentor Aldous's cottage, Theo finds letters revealing the ember of war-magic was placed inside them as a child—the reason the valley was chosen, the reason magic cannot follow there. Emotional beat: grief reframed as betrayal; identity shaken at its foundation.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren Calloway, a disgraced royal mapmaker hiding in Hollowmere, offers Theo a smuggler's route out—repaying a debt to Aldous. Their escape plan collapses when Vess takes hostages among the villagers. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; Wren's cynicism cracking against Theo's stubborn decency.

chapters.title: A Child Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo and Wren flee with Pip, a mute orphan whose drawings depict the ancient war in impossible detail—she carries memory like a wound. Vess's hunters close in; a bridge burns behind them. Emotional beat: found family forming in flight, fragile and unspoken.

chapters.title: The Oathbreakers' Road
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. On the old war-road, the trio shelters with a hidden community of oath-breakers—mages who renounced their gifts to survive. An elder tests Theo and recoils from the ember's heat. Pip speaks her first word: Theo's name. Emotional beat: belonging offered, then complicated by fear of what Theo carries.

chapters.title: Vess Arden's Truth
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Interlude reveals her motive: she lost her family to a swordspeaker's waking during the last flare of the war, and the crown promised her the ember's destruction—or its weaponization, whichever serves them. She doubts the crown; she does not doubt her grief. Emotional beat: antagonist humanized; vengeance revealed as another kind of mourning.

chapters.title: The Spoken Blade
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Cornered at the ruins of the first battlefield, Theo is forced to speak a partial oath to save Pip, waking one blade—and feeling the ember strain toward full waking. Wren is gravely wounded shielding them. Emotional beat: terror of one's own power; love made concrete through sacrifice.

chapters.title: Emberfall
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. At the crown's siege camp, Theo confronts Vess before the assembled army. Instead of fighting, Theo begins the new oath—unbinding the ember and scattering its fire into every blade present, so no single hand can ever wield the old war again. Vess chooses, at the last, not to stop them. Emotional beat: surrender as victory; grief and release entwined.

chapters.title: A Home With No Walls
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, epilogue-like. Magicless now, Theo returns to a changed Hollowmere with Wren (healing) and Pip (speaking freely). The valley's ward has dissolved; travelers come and go; Theo teaches children ordinary swordwork and extraordinary honesty. Emotional beat: resolution—identity rebuilt not around the gift, but around the people who stayed.
